s: Der Zerfall des Römerreiches raubte der Stadt Rom die alte Stellung als Mittelpunkt alles Geschehens.
The decay of the Roman empire robbed the city of Rome of the old position as the center of all that was happening.
town (a settlement larger than a village)
city center (a central business area of a city)
city, town, town council, city council (a governing body of people elected to oversee management of a municipality)

s: strong (having a high concentration of some ingredient, e.g. alcohol)
Nun, es sind Eheleute, in Gottes Namen, soweit ist die Sache in Ordnung. Aber am hellen Morgen, das ist doch stark.
Well, they are a married couple, in God's name, there's no issue in that regard. But in right in the bright of morning, unbelievable, really.
strong (inflecting according to a pattern distinct from another called "weak")
stark.et: From Middle High German starc, from Old High German stark, from Proto-West Germanic *stark.

s: country, state (politically constituted legal person wielding absolute power of a population and territory)
state/government, authorities (the entire political and administrative system of such an entity)
1932, Erich Mühsam, Die Befreiung der Gesellschaft vom Staat, in: Erich Mühsam: Prosaschriften II, Verlag europäische ideen Berlin (1978), page 253
Again and again we hear the question from people who are not familiar with the world of ideas of anarchism: What do you actually want? How do you imagine a society without state and authorities?
entourage of a sovereign or prince
stateliness; that which gives the effect of it; fine appearance in clothing and ménage
Staat.et: From Middle Low German stāt, from Middle Dutch staet, probably via Old French estat from Latin status. The semantic development was influenced by cognate modern French état. Doublet of Status and Etat.

s: Ihm ist, als ob es tausend Stäbe gäbe / und hinter tausend Stäben keine Welt.
Stab.et:
From Middle High German stap, stab, from Old High German stab, from Proto-West Germanic *stab.
Cognate with English staff, Dutch staf, Swedish stav, Old Norse stafr. The meaning co-workers is secondary: in the German word Generalstab (“General Staff”) the mean…

s: stalking (crime of following or harassing another person, causing him or her to fear death or injury)
stable, sty, shed, barn (building for keeping animals of all sorts); stall, sty (compartment within such a building); (loosely) pen (small outdoors area for keeping animals, properly Pferch)
synonym of Stelle, place something is situated, stead (occasionally with implication that something is “standing”, gestellt)
stale, i.e. the urine of horses or their act of urination (so called because they micturate, stallen, while standing, whereas they defecate in locomotion)
Stall.et: From Middle High German stal, from Old High German stal, from Proto-West Germanic *stall, from Proto-Germanic *stallaz.

s: class, stratum (group of people with a certain social status)
Dieser Fanatismus für die Kunst und insbesondere für die theatralische Kunst ging in Wien durch alle Stände.
An gut 100 Ständen präsentieren sich Vereine und Geschäfte, bieten die heimischen Gastronomen eine Auswahl ihrer Spezialitäten an.
At around 100 vendor booths you get local associations and businesses presenting themselves and restaurateurs offer their choice delicacies.
Stand.et: From Middle High German stant, from Old High German *stant (attested in Old High German firstant, urstant), from Proto-West Germanic *stand, a deverbal from *standan (“to stand”). Cognate with English stand.

Star.et:
From Middle High German star, stare, from Old High German stara, staro, star, from Proto-West Germanic *star.
Cognate with Middle Dutch sterre, Middle Low German stār(e), Old English stær, Old Norse stari, and further with Latin sturnus.

16th-century backformation from now archaic starblind, staarblind, from Middle High German star(e)blint, from Old High German starablint (“blind or highly vision-impaired but having normal-looking eyes”). The meaning is interpreted as "blind with cloudy eyes."…
19th century, from English star. Doublet of Aster and Stern.

s:
Gründlich durchgecheckt steht sie da
Und wartet auf den Start, alles klar

Thoroughly checked, [the rocket] stands there
And waits for the liftoff, all clear

Status.et: Learned borrowing from Latin status. Doublet of Staat and Etat.

s: pole; bar; rod; post (a long stick, usually round and of metal, but also of other material, especially when fixed somewhere)
small straight glass for beer (especially Kölsch)
a lot (especially of money); a packet
run-of-the-mill, chiefly with clothes (referring to the poles on which clothes are presented in large fashion shops)
Stangenkleidung ist mir nicht individuell genug.
I find run-of-the-mill garments lacking in individuality.
crossbar (the bar which conjoins two goalposts)
Stange.et: From Middle High German [Term?], from Old High German stanga, from Proto-Germanic *stangō. Compare English stang.

Stahl.et: From Middle High German stahel, from Old High German stahal, from Proto-Germanic *stahlą, *stahliją. Cognate with Dutch staal, Danish stål, Icelandic stál, also English steel.

s: needle bug, water stick insect (insect genus Ranatra).

Stachelbeere.et: Stachel + Beere (“berry”). The term has been attested since at least the late 16th century; the 1607 dictionary Dictionnaire François-Allemand & Allemand-François contains the variant forms "Stachelbeer" and "Stichelbeer".

s: Ein Kaktus hat keine Stacheln, sondern Dornen, während eine Rose keine Dornen, sondern Stacheln hat.
A cactus has no spines, only thorns, while a rose has prickles but no thorns.
Stachel.et: From Middle High German stachel, from Late Old High German stahhil, from Old High German stakulla, from an extension of stechen with nominalizing suffix -ila.

Stachelschwein.et: 16th century, from Stachel (“spine, spike”) + Schwein (“pig, swine”), a calque of Latin porcus spīnōsus, itself a calque of Ancient Greek ἀκανθόχοιρος (akanthókhoiros).

s: skewer (pin used to secure food during cooking)
Er isst Reis am liebsten mit Stäbchen.
He prefers eating rice with chopsticks.
Stalin (assumed name of Soviet ruler, Joseph Stalin, né Djugashvili)
Stalin.et: Borrowed from Russian Ста́лин (Stálin), from сталь (stalʹ, “steel”), itself from German Stahl (“steel”).

s: Statt mich anzurufen, ging er mit seinen Freunden ins Kino.
Instead of calling me, he went to the movies with his friends.
Der Wettbewerb findet am Mittwoch statt.
The competition takes place on Wednesday.

Stärke.et: From Middle High German sterke, from Old High German starchī. By surface analysis, stark (“strong”) + -e.

Stätte.et: From Middle High German stat, from Old High German stat, from Proto-West Germanic *stadi, from Proto-Germanic *stadiz. Doublet of Statt and Stadt.

Staub.et:
From Middle High German stoup, stoub from Old High German stoub, from Proto-West Germanic *staub, from Proto-Germanic *staubaz, related to *steubaną (“to smoke, fume, fly about”) (compare also Gestüpp). Related to stieben.
Cognate with Danish støv, Norwegian B…

to accumulate, to build up, to get backed up
Wegen der Baustelle ist eine Spur gesperrt, deshalb staut sich hier der Verkehr.

Berlin gilt weltweit als attraktiver Standort für ein neues Startup.
Berlin is considered an attractive location worldwide for a new startup.
Viele Startups konzentrieren sich auf digitale Geschäftsmodelle.
Many startups focus on digital business models.
sovereign wealth fund (a state-owned investment fund that invests in real and financial assets)
Der norwegische Staatsfonds gilt als einer der größten und erfolgreichsten weltweit.
The Norwegian sovereign wealth fund is considered one of the largest and most successful worldwide.
Viele Länder nutzen einen Staatsfonds, um Einnahmen aus Rohstoffen für künftige Generationen anzulegen.
Many countries use a sovereign wealth fund to invest revenue from raw materials for future generations.
sovereign wealth fund (a more formal or technical term for a state-owned investment fund)
Der Begriff Staatsvermögensfonds betont den Charakter des Fonds als Teil des nationalen Kapitals.
The term sovereign wealth fund emphasizes the fund's character as part of the national capital.
International werden die Strategien großer Staatsvermögensfonds genau beobachtet.
Internationally, the strategies of large sovereign wealth funds are closely monitored.
Staatsvermögensfonds.et: Staat (“state”) + -s- (“genitival interfix”) + Vermögen (“assets; wealth”) + -s- (“genitival interfix”) + Fonds (“fund”)

s: stabilization fund (a fund established by a government to insulate the budget and economy from fluctuations in revenue, especially from commodity exports)
Der Stabilisierungsfonds dient dazu, bei sinkenden Rohstoffpreisen Haushaltslöcher zu stopfen.
The stabilization fund serves to plug budget holes when commodity prices fall.
Während der Finanzkrise wurden staatliche Stabilisierungsfonds zur Rettung systemrelevanter Banken eingesetzt.
During the financial crisis, state stabilization funds were used to rescue systemically important banks.
state assets; public wealth (all assets owned by a state, including financial reserves, infrastructure, and land)
Zum Staatsvermögen zählen nicht nur Goldreserven, sondern auch öffentliche Gebäude und Infrastruktur.
State assets include not only gold reserves, but also public buildings and infrastructure.
Die Verwaltung des Staatsvermögens obliegt oft speziellen Behörden oder Ministerien.
The management of state assets is often the responsibility of special authorities or ministries.
sovereign debt crisis (a period of time in which a country is unable to pay back its government debt)
Die Staatsschuldenkrise zwang viele Regierungen zu drastischen Sparmaßnahmen.
The sovereign debt crisis forced many governments to take drastic austerity measures.
Ein Schuldenschnitt wurde als letztes Mittel zur Bewältigung der Staatsschuldenkrise diskutiert.
A debt haircut was discussed as a last resort for managing the sovereign debt crisis.
public spending ratio (total government expenditure to GDP ratio)
debt-to-GDP ratio (total government debt in percent of GDP)
dust catcher; something that is rarely used and catches dust
Spazierenzufahren war unmöglich, weil das Deichselpferd stätisch war und in der Gabeldeichsel ausschlug.
Im Schein der winzigen Lampenflamme ließen sie sich nieder, auf kleine Stabellen die beiden Mädchen, rund um sie auf dem Boden die Schüler.
Stabelle.et: Variant of Schabelle, ultimately from Latin scabellum (“footstool”). Doublet of Schemel.

s: communal kitchen (run by a municipality that caters community facilities like day care centers, retirement homes, nursing homes, etc.)
City of Brussels (the largest municipality of Brussels, Brussels Capital Region, Belgium)
urban express railway, suburban commuter rail system
Die Stadtschnellbahn verbindet die Außenbezirke mit dem Stadtzentrum.
The urban express railway connects the outer districts with the city center.
In vielen Städten wird die Stadtschnellbahn kurz S-Bahn genannt.
In many cities, the urban express railway is called S-Bahn for short.
light rail, urban railway (a passenger transit system using rail vehicles, often intermediate between a tramway and a metro)
Die neue Stadtbahn verbindet das Zentrum mit den östlichen Vororten.
The new light rail connects the center with the eastern suburbs.
Viele Städte haben ihre alte Straßenbahn zu einer modernen Stadtbahn umgebaut.
Many cities have converted their old tramway system into a modern light rail system.
Stapelfeld (a municipality of Stormarn district, Schleswig-Holstein, Germany)
Stapelfeld.et: By surface analysis, Stapel (“stack, batch”) + Feld (“field”). Cognate with English Staplefield.
